candidate.answerReason: The oddness identity gives sin(-90°)=-sin90°=-1, consistent with the unit-circle point (0,-1).

methods.label: Use sine's oddness
methods.explanation: Sine is an odd function, so \(\sin(-90°)=-\sin90°=-1\).
methods.levelReason: Uses odd-function symmetry and the standard value sin90°=1 within the required high-school scope.

methods.label: Locate the negative angle
methods.explanation: A negative angle turns clockwise, so a \(90°\) clockwise turn from the positive \(x\)-axis reaches the unit-circle point \((0,-1)\). Sine is the \(y\)-coordinate of this point, so \(\sin(-90°)=-1\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the earlier unit-circle definition and negative-angle convention directly, without requiring function parity.
